chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Other leaders with good bands: Lloyd Reese, Marvin Johnson, Snake White
summary: Howard says only Lloyd Reese did important band work; Marvin Johnson had a good band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Any of these people at the time, were they doing anything of importance, you know, where you remember somebody having a band that you liked or somebody like Bumps Meyers or somebody through that period that was --
He was one of the only ones doing the important things?
He was playing and doing -- he'd just play the band pieces right through, you know?
Uh-huh. What about Marvin Johnson? Did he ever have his own band or anything?
No, he never had his own band, but he played with bands.
He had a trombone, you know.
Marvin was a saxophone player, though.
You've got me twisted up here now.
I can't pull you out of that one. I know Happy didn't play -- you was talking about Happy Johnson?

Yeah, at first I was talking about Happy Johnson, and you said you didn't remember other than him just jamming. Now we were talking about Marvin Johnson, whether he had his own band. He was a saxophone player.
Oh, Marvin had his own band.
Yeah, I wondered if he had a band.
A good band. A good band.
Anybody else that you remember had a good band in Los Angeles around that period we're talking about?
Snake White. Oh, Snake come back and played with all the bands.
Did he have his own band too that you know of?

Yeah, he came and played with all the bands. In other words he would set up, you know, his own composition and so forth, and bands would play it. But that's the only thing Snake did. Snake didn't do anything that would hurt anybody.
